answer: Subtree-disjoint review quorums. Every identity hangs from an invite-tree anchor, and each epoch it must review 5 tasks, each from a different invite subtree. Task payloads are sealed under a cipher key held only by the author and a verifier, so reviews can't be copied. Tasks are drawn at random from a nebula, the pool of all open tasks, so a farm can't pick its own. A review counts only if it matches the verifier's re-run. Cost per fake: 5 real re-runs, about 15 compute-minutes per epoch, so 500 fakes need 2,500 re-runs, and one farm subtree fills one slot.
